## Assignment Simulated Data

### 1. Load Cytokine Dataset

```{r}
olink_inflammation_cytokines_1000 = read.csv("olink_inflammation_cytokines_1000.csv")
```

### 2. Simulate values for HD and Disease

`Olink-like NPX values (log2 scale). Each protein gets its own baseline level and its own biological variation. Across all proteins and subjects, the values have a mean of about 4 and an SD of about 2.`

```{r}

set.seed(1)

# Defining dataset
n = 30      # Sample size
ng = 2      # Number of groups
p = 1000    # Number of variables

# Baseline level: some are abundant, some low
mu_p = rnorm(p, mean = 4, sd = 1.7)

# Biological variation between subjects
sd_p = runif(p, min = 0.6, max = 1.4)

# Putting data into a matrix
data = matrix(0, nrow = p, ncol = n*ng)
for (i in 1:p){
  data[i,] = rnorm(n*ng, mean = mu_p[i], sd = sd_p[i])
}

# Add column and row names to df
colnames(data) = c(paste("HD", 1:n, sep=""), paste("Disease", 1:n, sep=""))
rownames(data) = olink_inflammation_cytokines_1000$Assay
head(data)

# check overall distribution of the data, should be approx mean 4 and sd 2
mean(data)
sd(data)
hist(data, col = "grey", main = "All simulated NPX values", xlab = "NPX")

# columns of each group
hd_cols  = 1:n
dis_cols = (n + 1):(n * ng)
```

### 3. Increase SD and values in Disease

All proteins get a slightly larger SD in the Disease group, leaving patients as more heterogeneous. Ten well-known inflammation markers get higher levels. How much higher depends on each patient's disease severity, so the markers rise together, as inflammatory proteins tend to do. Acute-phase proteins (CRP, SAA1) rise the most.

```{r}
set.seed(2)                                   # separate seed for the manipulation

# Mean NPX increase in disease per marker (proteins not listed stay at 0)
marker_shift = c("IL-6"           = 2.5,
                 "TNF"            = 2.0,
                 "IL-1 beta"      = 2.0,
                 "IL-8"           = 2.0,
                 "CRP"            = 3.5,
                 "SAA1"           = 3.5,
                 "Calprotectin"   = 2.5,
                 "CXCL10 (IP-10)" = 2.0,
                 "CCL2 (MCP-1)"   = 2.0,
                 "IFN-gamma"      = 2.0)
all(names(marker_shift) %in% rownames(data))   # check that names are same

delta = marker_shift[rownames(data)]                    # NA for unlisted proteins
delta[is.na(delta)] = 0
delta = as.numeric(delta)

# Protein-to-protein variability around the marker shift
up = delta > 0
delta[up] = delta[up] + rnorm(sum(up), mean = 0, sd = 0.3)

# Disease severity per patient: 0.5 = mild, 1.5 = severe
severity = runif(n, min = 0.5, max = 1.5)

# Apply shift + inflate SD in the Disease group
sd_mult = 1.2                    # SD inflation for all Disease values 

dis      = data[, dis_cols]
dis_mean = rowMeans(dis)         # each protein's own disease mean

# Scale deviations around the protein mean (means stay put), then add the shift
dis = dis_mean + (dis - dis_mean) * sd_mult + outer(delta, severity)
data[, dis_cols] = dis

# Ground truth for validation
truth = data.frame(Protein   = rownames(data),
                   TrueDelta = delta,
                   Up        = up)
truth[truth$Up, ]


# Used further down in the answer key and review
inflam      = rownames(data)[up]
inflam_rows = which(up)
```

### 4. Introduce biomarkers and errors

```         
Besides the univariate biomarkers and the two errors, three things are built in to be harder to find:

-   Combination marker (4.3): 
Two proteins share a large patient-to-patient variation, so on their own they barely differ between the groups and won't stand out in a volcano plot. Their ratio (their difference on the log2 NPX scale) separates the groups well. It takes a multivariate method, or looking at protein pairs, to find it.

-   Subgroup marker (4.4): 
IL-17A is strongly raised in only 8 of the 30 Disease patients (an "IL-17-high" disease subtype). Averaged over all disease patients the difference is not very clear, so a t-test is unlikely to flag it after FDR correction, but the subgroup is visible in a boxplot or heatmap.

-   Misdiagnosed patient (4.6):
The mildest disease patient is labelled as HD. Its inflammation markers are only slightly raised, so it is hard to tell apart from a healthy donor.
```

```{r}

# 4.1 True diagnosis
group = c(rep("HD", n), rep("Disease", n))

# 4.2 Introduce 10 biomarkers
n_bio = 10

# Randomly select 10 proteins among synthetic ones (so they don't overlap with inflammation markers from section 3)
synthetic = which(olink_inflammation_cytokines_1000$Data_Source == "Synthetic placeholder")
biomarkers = sample(synthetic, n_bio)

# Effects in Disease group
fc = c(4, 3, 3, 2, 2, -4, -3, -3, -2, -2)

for (k in 1:n_bio) {
  data[biomarkers[k], dis_cols] =
    data[biomarkers[k], dis_cols] + fc[k]
}

# Display selected biomarkers
biomarker_names = rownames(data)[biomarkers]
biomarker_names

# 4.3 Introduce a combination marker (two proteins whose ratio differs)
combo = sample(setdiff(synthetic, biomarkers), 2)
combo_names = rownames(data)[combo]

shared = rnorm(n*ng, mean = 0, sd = 1.8)      # Variation shared by both proteins

data[combo[1],] = mu_p[combo[1]] + shared + rnorm(n*ng, mean = 0, sd = 0.3)
data[combo[2],] = mu_p[combo[2]] + shared + rnorm(n*ng, mean = 0, sd = 0.3)
data[combo[2], dis_cols] = data[combo[2], dis_cols] + 1   # Ratio is 2x higher in Disease

combo_names

# 4.4 Introduce a subgroup marker: IL-17A high in 8 of the 30 Disease patients
sub_marker = "IL-17A"
sub_marker %in% rownames(data) # check to see it's not misspelled

n_sub = 8
mildest = dis_cols[which.min(severity)]       # Kept out: this patient gets misdiagnosed in 4.6
subgroup = sample(setdiff(dis_cols, mildest), n_sub)

data[sub_marker, subgroup] = data[sub_marker, subgroup] + 3

# 4.5 Introduce one outlier patient
outlier = sample(hd_cols, 1)

data[, outlier] = data[, outlier] + 3

# 4.6 Introduce one misdiagnosed patient (mildest disease patient)
misdiag = mildest

group_obs = group
group_obs[misdiag] = "HD"

# Display the problematic patients
colnames(data)[outlier]
colnames(data)[misdiag]
colnames(data)[subgroup]
```

### 5. Export dataset

Patients as rows, the group (A/B) as the first column, then the 1000 proteins. The row order is shuffled and the patient names are left out, so the labels can't be guessed.

```{r}
group_AB = ifelse(group_obs == "HD", "A", "B")   # A = HD, B = Disease

ord = sample(1:(n*ng))                           # Shuffle patient order
df = data.frame(group = group_AB[ord], t(data)[ord, ], check.names = FALSE)
write.csv(df, "simulated_dataset.csv", row.names = FALSE)

dim(df)                                          # Should be 60 x 1001
table(df$group)
```

### 6. Answer key

Summary of the specifics in the dataset

```{r}

# Proteins with a true difference between the groups
truth_proteins = data.frame(
  Protein    = c(inflam, biomarker_names, combo_names, sub_marker),
  Type       = c(rep("Inflammation marker", length(inflam)),
                 rep("Biomarker", n_bio),
                 rep("Combination pair (ratio)", 2),
                 "Subgroup marker (8 of 30 Disease)"),
  Effect_NPX = c(round(delta[inflam_rows], 2), fc, 0, 1, 3))  # Inflammation markers: average patient
# Combination pair: ratio is 2x (1 NPX) higher in Disease
truth_proteins

# Patients: true group, label in the file and row number in the file
truth_patients = data.frame(
  Patient       = colnames(data),
  True_group    = ifelse(group == "HD", "A", "B"),
  Label_in_file = group_AB,
  Row_in_file   = match(1:(n*ng), ord),
  Outlier       = 1:(n*ng) == outlier,
  Mislabelled   = group != group_obs,
  IL17_subgroup = 1:(n*ng) %in% subgroup)
truth_patients[truth_patients$Outlier | truth_patients$Mislabelled | truth_patients$IL17_subgroup, ]

write.csv(truth_proteins, "answer_key_proteins.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(truth_patients, "answer_key_patients.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

### 7. Quick review

Quick checks that the simulation behaves as intended, using the TRUE groups.

```{r}
# t-tests for all proteins (Welch's t-test, since Disease has a larger SD)
pval = NULL
for (i in 1:p){
  pval[i] = t.test(data[i,] ~ factor(group))$p.value
}
hist(pval, col = "grey")
padj = p.adjust(pval, method = "BH")
rownames(data)[padj < 0.05]                      # Should be the 20 univariate markers

# Combination pair: weak on their own, strong as a ratio
padj[combo]
t.test((data[combo[2],] - data[combo[1],]) ~ factor(group))$p.value
plot(data[combo[1],], data[combo[2],], col = ifelse(group == "HD", "blue", "red"), pch = 16,
     xlab = combo_names[1], ylab = combo_names[2], main = "Combination pair")

# Subgroup marker: not significant overall, but 8 patients clearly high
padj[rownames(data) == sub_marker]
stripchart(data[sub_marker,] ~ factor(group, levels = c("HD", "Disease")), vertical = TRUE,
           method = "jitter", pch = 16, col = c("blue", "red"), 
           ylab = paste(sub_marker, "(NPX)"))

# PCA: the two groups should separate
pca = prcomp(t(data))
plot(pca$x[,1], pca$x[,2], col = ifelse(group == "HD", "blue", "red"), pch = 16,
     xlab = "PC1", ylab = "PC2", main = "True groups (blue = HD, red = Disease)")

# PCA without the outlier: the mislabelled patient (black ring) sits among the disease patients
pca2 = prcomp(t(data[, -outlier]))
plot(pca2$x[,1], pca2$x[,2], col = ifelse(group[-outlier] == "HD", "blue", "red"), pch = 16,
     xlab = "PC1", ylab = "PC2", main = "Without the outlier")
points(pca2$x[colnames(data)[misdiag],1], pca2$x[colnames(data)[misdiag],2], cex = 2)

# Sample boxplots: the outlier patient should stand out
boxplot(data, las = 2, cex.axis = 0.6, outline = FALSE,
        col = ifelse(1:(n*ng) == outlier, "red", "grey"))

# What the other group will see: CRP by the labels in the file
# The mislabelled patient (red point) does NOT stand out on CRP alone
boxplot(data["CRP",] ~ group_AB, col = c("lightblue", "salmon"),
        xlab = "Label in file (A = HD, B = Disease)", ylab = "CRP (NPX)")
points(1, data["CRP", misdiag], col = "red", pch = 16)

# ...but it does on the combined inflammation markers (mean of the 10 markers)
inflam_score = colMeans(data[inflam_rows, -outlier])
boxplot(inflam_score ~ group_AB[-outlier], col = c("lightblue", "salmon"),
        xlab = "Label in file (A = HD, B = Disease)", ylab = "Mean of inflammation markers (NPX)")
points(1, inflam_score[colnames(data)[misdiag]], col = "red", pch = 16)
```
